batch_strategy: Select 32 condition gaps that distinguish scaffold-specific response curves, endpoint-specific loading associations, and transfer from exceptional records. Use linked experiments where they resolve a concrete ambiguity, with broader coverage of sparsely measured carbonyl environments and early amine responses. All selected IDs and supplied premeasurement predictions are frozen before any new labels are revealed.

choices.reason: m63 at 5/1 and 100 uL starts a fixed-loading cyclic-ketone curve. Its measured 10/1 anchor, c65455de87b41e2ef577, is 6.07/17.80 mL. The selected 20/1 and 50/1 points will determine whether the methyl-substituted ring environment changes transition location relative to tetralone.

m63 at 20/1 and 100 uL is the central point of that curve, predicted at 9.66/23.49 mL. Tetralone measured 13.52/30.38 mL at this ratio in 1668026caa5d708642cf. The comparison can constrain structural transfer, while differing molecules and loading amounts prevent treating it as a controlled methyl-substitution effect.

m63 at 50/1 completes the fixed-loading curve. Its 16.11/34.18 mL forecast lies between the measured weak-eluent responses of related ring ketones in a36291cab664852df5e5 and 52348febee6695107c49. This tests whether the predictor places late-ratio growth appropriately in a sparsely measured ring environment.

m64 at 5/1 and 100 uL extends its measured 1/1 baseline, c4c10cf623fbb8793829f, toward the selected 20/1 condition. This brominated propiophenone provides a useful test of carbonyl connectivity and substitution-position transfer without presuming the stronger response of brominated acetophenones.

m64 at 20/1 and 100 uL tests the modest 6.83/18.58 mL forecast. Related brominated acetophenones have appreciable weak-eluent growth, including 605436d35600502e8c2e and a6f8e492c9e561c79cbd. Together with the selected 5/1 point, this label can distinguish a genuinely flatter scaffold response from excessive shrinkage.

m40 at 10/1 and 50 uL supplies the lower-loading counterpart to 1a382a7d3a13ed7fb28f, measured at 12.87/24.12 mL with 150 uL. It also anchors the selected low-loading 20/1 point, testing where loading-associated onset differences appear before the established 50/1 growth.

m40 at 20/1 and 50 uL fills the segment before its measured 50/1 result, 8b9ff1a26d840aaa6a49. The recent high-loading 50/1 result, 4e93e36ab850bab3d594, rejected the forecast of a large contraction. This intermediate label locates curvature instead of acquiring another nearly bracketed 50/1 loading point.

m186 at 20/1 and 50 uL completes a loading contrast with 5f1ae4e354b8b36ec691 and 14636dfc9018393d202e. The high-loading onset stayed near 5 mL from 20/1 to 50/1, whereas the measured low-loading 50/1 onset was 13.49 mL. This tests where those curves diverge.

m186 at 50/1 and 100 uL fills the loading midpoint between 5bf4578bc08db91b5967 and c45057c2cab40f4fa2be. Their onsets differ by about 8.4 mL while completions differ by only about 1.1 mL. The midpoint distinguishes gradual onset change from a more localized transition.

Terephthalaldehyde at 5/1 and 150 uL completes the loading series with 20711ea4080ba078e890 and b8c35c514f5ef6c0f3bc. Those lower-loading observations differ in opposite directions for onset and completion. The label tests whether that endpoint separation persists at the upper loading rather than moving both endpoints together.

Dibenzoylmethane at 50/1, 100 uL and 300 uL DCM fills the midpoint between 5f02dc3c13f7f2daed32 and e82a87ee526fdd9b1e8d. Their onsets are 10.57 versus 5.34 mL, with much smaller completion differences. Matching the recorded loading-solvent volume makes this a particularly useful endpoint-specific loading contrast.

Benzyl benzoate at 30/1 and 150 uL tests transfer from the low-loading 30/1 observation 704ba630f25fe7f20166. The measured high-loading 20/1 anchor c0c1e5902a4bf388fcd0 already has later completion than that low-loading 30/1 record. This point helps distinguish loading associations from local response curvature.

Benzyl benzoate at 100/1 and 150 uL tests extrapolation from 7f4f64cb791c71ba0420 at 50 uL and the recent 50/1 midpoint 54d9921472c8d46b7b9a. It asks whether completion continues growing at high loading or whether the narrow low-loading 100/1 interval transfers across loading.

Ethyl 2-bromopropionate at 2/1 and 50 uL tests whether the late, nearly coincident high-loading endpoints in 308ffc82485e086c1c09 extend to lower loading. Its measured low-loading 1/1 and 20/1 references are ordinary. This label can prevent an exceptional tuple from inducing a molecule-wide correction.

The same ester at 2/1 and 100 uL adds the midpoint to the selected 50 uL condition and measured 150 uL condition 308ffc82485e086c1c09. The predictor gives nearly identical forecasts across these loadings. Two new labels can distinguish a localized high-loading record from a broader onset change.

m57 at 50/1 and 50 uL tests loading transfer from 63ec73e3341feaaf43ae, whose 150 uL endpoints were approximately 16.05/16.08 mL. A lipophilic donor-free arene provides a useful comparison outside polar families. Chemical expectations favor limited silica interaction, but do not establish that the exceptional record is erroneous.

m29 under pure EA at 100 uL is predicted at 4.37/16.48 mL, compared with measured 1/1 endpoints of 4.28/8.77 mL in a7a30ef771295dc6deed. This directly tests a predicted completion reversal at an uncovered boundary for a sterically crowded aromatic ketone.

Dimethylbenzonitrile m130 under pure EA at 100 uL tests the predicted completion near 16.85 mL. Its measured 1/1 completions are about 8 mL in 2d27f02deb37eeb61bfe and efb7617d566fb19d9217. This determines whether the strong-eluent maximum is real recorded behavior or inappropriate transfer from other methylated aromatics.

Fluorenone at 1/1 and 150 uL tests a concrete predicted trough: completion is forecast at 12.61 mL, versus measured 20.41 mL under pure EA in 9948433906d4afa41345 and 22.94 mL at 5/1 in d7603686249e1fb69a60. These anchors share the selected loading conditions.

Fluorenone at 10/1 and 150 uL fills the fixed-loading gap between d7603686249e1fb69a60 at 5/1 and 204c95299f49a2bcdb61 at 20/1. It tests whether completion grows while onset remains early, complementing the selected 1/1 trough test without requiring a uniform correction to both endpoints.

m23 at 20/1 and 150 uL extends the measured 5/1 result 90ae8e9fe447f6a79598, which repaired a predicted endpoint-ordering failure. The actual observed-table record fda75f6050d42df09e91 belongs to m121 at 2/1, so m23's intended 20/1 test remains uncovered.

Ethyl p-methoxybenzoate at 10/1 and 100 uL joins the selected 50 uL point and measured 150 uL result ef809aee1c6b06021475. The current completion forecast is about 17.54 mL, below that high-loading measurement of 21.79 mL. This tests endpoint-specific loading transfer at an intermediate ratio.

m23 at 50/1 and 100 uL tests the forecast of 9.64/14.35 mL against the short measured 10/1 endpoints in cef2e794508403355c31 at the same loading. It extends the response test to weaker eluent and constrains a common short-retention region without relying on large predicted volumes.

The fluorobenzyl cyclopropyl ketone m172 at 2/1 supplies an early anchor before its measured 20/1 and 50/1 records fd11ee7c408d95a1a8e6 and 419f6eb4080dcb9d293b. Its nonconjugated carbonyl environment offers a useful test of response transfer from the more extensively measured directly aryl-bound ketones.

Cyanobenzophenone at 20/1 and 150 uL bridges the measured 10/1 and 50/1 endpoints in 79ff49052bce33597828 and 1395836aef00d6a880b0. Its predicted completion of 44.31 mL is also below both lower-loading 20/1 measurements. This tests loading transfer within a well-defined steep response segment.

Ethyl p-methoxybenzoate at 10/1 and 50 uL fills the low-loading interval between c449ecc5ee6acf61bddb at 5/1 and eed75e5b0d9c27fa754c at 20/1. Together with the selected midpoint and existing high-loading label, it tests whether onset and completion have different loading dependence during this transition.

p-Methoxybenzophenone at 10/1 and 50 uL locates the beginning of its loading-associated onset differences. Measurements at 20/1 and 50/1, including d035281432e410405550 and 2d63ab3869184cde52bf, show earlier onset at higher loading with relatively similar completion. The 10/1 label tests where that association becomes appreciable.

Methoxyethyl acrylate at 2/1 and 50 uL fills an uncovered early-ratio point after the measured 1/1 condition 66e8febca8812396280d. It connects that lower-loading anchor to the measured 5/1 and 10/1 response, helping distinguish the extra ether's condition response from that of simpler acrylates.

Methoxyethyl acrylate at 5/1 and 150 uL supplies a loading contrast to c86b03e1b275528444a6 at 100 uL. The current forecast changes little from that measured midpoint. This tests whether loading insensitivity is appropriate for this ether-ester environment, rather than transferring stronger loading associations from alcohols or beta-ketoesters.

Dibenzylamine at 1/1 and 50 uL starts a fixed-loading early-response experiment with the selected 2/1 condition. Existing 0/1 and 5/1 records 18a189c89f59ac1d5a9f and d5234e966aa231be05e5 have modest endpoints. This constrains the early curve before the much larger measured 10/1 response at other loadings.

Dibenzylamine at 2/1 and 50 uL completes that early-response experiment and contrasts with 6defbf00ecb558b77d50 at 100 uL. It tests whether the shorter measured low-loading 5/1 result reflects a local reversal, a loading association, or variability that the predictor should avoid spreading across the entire basic scaffold.

2,6-Dimethylpyridine at 1/1 and 50 uL fills an early-ratio gap before its measured 5/1-to-10/1 growth. Records 74c8fcd8ac3f6caedcd2 and 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0 establish substantial later response. The label tests the strong-eluent transition for a sterically shielded basic nitrogen environment alongside the selected secondary amine experiment.

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading associations depend on molecule and PE/EA and can move onset and completion differently. Recent results favor learning these interactions locally; they do not support a universal loading shift or establish that every contrast is caused by loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many candidate forecasts barely change across loading. Matched loading series and linked ratio points can teach when that insensitivity is appropriate and when onset and completion require separate responses. Unrecorded factors remain a limitation on causal interpretation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m186 and dibenzoylmethane loading midpoints interpolate smoothly, and do the ester, dialdehyde and methoxybenzophenone contrasts retain endpoint-specific associations at their selected ratios?

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response curvature and endpoint coupling are scaffold-specific. Strong growth in one carbonyl environment should not induce a uniform correction across related ketones, esters or other acceptor-containing structures.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The recent m40 underprediction and m115 overprediction have opposite directions, while several other carbonyl forecasts were close. Missing curve points can locate transitions and improve structural transfer without imposing universal monotonicity or a family-wide offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do m63 and m64 develop retention growth, and do the selected m40, fluorenone, m172 and cyanobenzophenone points preserve their scaffold-specific onset/completion relationships?

hypotheses.content: The nearly coincident endpoint records for m77 at 2/1 and m57 at 50/1 may be localized to their recorded conditions rather than representing molecule-wide behavior. The m186 follow-up shows why transfer from such a record requires independent condition evidence.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A single unusual label can distort nearby predictions when loading sensitivity is weak. Lower-loading and midpoint labels can delimit the appropriate scope of that transfer. These comparisons cannot by themselves identify an unrecorded mechanism or prove a measurement error.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are m77's 50 and 100 uL 2/1 endpoints ordinary or progressively late, and does m57's low-loading 50/1 record reproduce the late onset seen at 150 uL?

hypotheses.content: Completion reversals near the pure-EA boundary can occur in the recorded data, but their transfer to other scaffolds remains unresolved. The predicted pure-EA maxima for m29 and m130 and the predicted 1/1 trough for fluorenone require direct labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These measurements discriminate real recorded boundary behavior from inappropriate transfer of reversals. They can improve strong-eluent predictions without assuming that conventional solvent-strength expectations must hold for every catalog record.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m29 and m130 actually finish later under pure EA than at 1/1, and does fixed-loading fluorenone have the pronounced completion trough predicted at 1/1?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest m40 result weakened the predicted large loading contraction: at 50/1 and 150 uL it measured 37.14/67.02 mL, with historical acquisition errors of -10.41/-17.35 mL. I therefore select earlier curve gaps rather than another 50/1 midpoint, whose current forecast has already moved toward the measured endpoints. In the opposite direction, m115 at 10/1 and 50 uL measured 9.84/17.50 mL, substantially shorter in completion than its historical forecast. Together these outcomes argue against a blanket carbonyl correction.

m186 at high loading retained onset near 5 mL from 20/1 to 50/1 while completion increased. Its low-loading 50/1 onset was much later, motivating two targeted loading/ratio gaps. The terephthalaldehyde results likewise support endpoint-specific comparisons. The accurate iodophenol midpoint, ordinary m190 2/1 outcome, and modest errors for several benzophenone, cyclic-ketone and lipophilic records reduce the value of further nearby baseline measurements. The lower-loading methyl-anthranilate early curve was comparatively well predicted, so I shift attention to less-covered early amine environments.

I use the observed-table metadata when it conflicts with the previous selection narrative: fda75f6050d42df09e91 is m121 at 2/1, and therefore does not establish m23's planned 20/1 response. Historical errors above are acquisition-time feedback, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The batch contains 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs, with no pending experiments and no duplicate molecule-condition tuples within the selection. It combines failure follow-up with condition coverage that can teach relationships shared by many rows. The m63 three-point curve and m64 pair expand sparsely measured aromatic-ketone environments. The m40, fluorenone, m172 and cyanobenzophenone selections locate response transitions using existing anchors rather than simply seeking large retention volumes.

Loading experiments address concrete endpoint ambiguities: m186 and dibenzoylmethane have large observed onset contrasts with much smaller completion contrasts; terephthalaldehyde and several aromatic esters test how those associations change with scaffold and ratio. The m77 pair and m57 point delimit transfer from nearly coincident endpoint records. The pure-EA and fluorenone boundary experiments discriminate predicted reversals, while m23 constrains short-retention predictions after its ordering failure. The early dibenzylamine and dimethylpyridine measurements add useful coverage of basic silica-interacting environments without assuming a common amine correction.

These labels may improve overall Row accuracy by teaching where structural and loading transfer succeeds, where it fails, and how V1 and V2 respond separately. Cross-molecule comparisons are informative analogies, not controlled substitution experiments. Missing experimental factors may explain some recorded contrasts. Quantile widths are treated as single-predictor outputs rather than calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 is treated only as the elution interval width.
